name: William Robinson
abstract: We can fixate on an object while attending to our visual periphery. It is difficult to describe how the world looks when we do this, and it is difficult to explain why such description is difficult. This paper focuses on these difficulties, with particular attention to the question whether they threaten realism about experiences. Several views are considered, including one that proposes that we have only partial access to our peripheral experience.
field: Philosophy of mind, philosophy of consciousness
notable: Author of 'Understanding Phenomenal Consciousness' (Cambridge University Press); developed Qualitative Event Realism
notes: Retired faculty. Long career in philosophy of mind.
